criteria.name: Introduction: mission concept and rationale. Include the following required information: What is the spacecraft's primary mission? Why is the mission needed? How many spacecraft are used and why? Who are the users (operator and customers)?
criteria.reasoning: Mission need, direct-detection rationale, single-spacecraft choice, operator and customers are all clearly explained with appropriate references. Strong introduction.

evidence.quote: The primary mission of ZYZZsat is to image the whole Great Barrier Reef in visible bands at 5 m resolution
The operator is the Australian Institute of Marine Science (AIMS)

criteria.name: Main body: mission design. Present a summary of the mission design using software and/or hand calculations as appropriate. Include relevant screenshots and software files in the main body of the report and/or appendix. Include the following information: Where will it launch from, and using which launch vehicle? Why did you choose this option? What type of orbit will you use? What are its characteristics and orbital elements? Will you need to perform any orbital maneuvers? Which ground control facilities will you use? How often will your spacecraft be able to communicate with ground control? How long will the mission last, and what are your plans for EOL?
criteria.reasoning: Launch, orbit elements, coverage, communications, manoeuvres, duration and EOL are comprehensively addressed with STK screenshots, tables and hand calculations. Minor weaknesses in revisit estimate and link budget do not prevent Accomplished.

evidence.quote: The most suitable orbit is a low-Earth sun-synchronous orbit
There are six passes each day, three in the evening and three in the morning (UTC)

criteria.name: Conclusion
criteria.reasoning: Conclusion summarises specific achieved performance and candidly identifies limitations and next steps. Detailed and evidence-based.

evidence.quote: ZYZZsat meets the mission needs set out in the introduction with one 50 kg satellite.

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Clear engineering-report structure, concise writing, labelled figures/tables and matching citations. Some bibliography entries are incomplete or weakly formatted, so not top of range.

evidence.quote: This report presents the design of ZYZZsat
The following STK 11 files are submitted with this report in ZYZZsat_STK.zip.

technical_issues.issue: Revisit-time calculation is a simple division of track spacing by roll-access width and is not demonstrated with an STK coverage/revisit analysis; it may be conservative or ambiguous.
No X-band link budget is presented; the 50 Mbit/s downlink and 34 min usable contact give an unverified 3.5 data margin.
Baseline Vega C was unflown at the report date, and rideshare injection dispersion cannot be corrected without propulsion; the delivered orbit may differ from 600 km and 97.79°.
Mount Pleasant is a radio astronomy/geodesy site; adding S-band and X-band capability is assumed without supporting evidence.

overall: Strong, concise report meeting all mission-design requirements. STK and hand calculations support launch, orbit, coverage, downlink and EOL. Minor weaknesses are the approximate revisit/roll calculation, missing X-band link budget, unflown Vega C baseline and assumed ground-station capability; these are acknowledged or limited in impact.

feedback.summary: You produced a strong, concise mission design that meets all requirements. STK and hand calculations support launch, orbit, coverage, downlink and EOL. Your Introduction and Conclusion are clear and well referenced. Main improvements: strengthen the revisit calculation, add an X-band link budget, address Vega C/rideshare and ground-station assumptions, and polish bibliography formatting.
next_steps: In §2.3/Table 3, replace or support the track-spacing/roll-width revisit estimate with an STK coverage/revisit analysis, stating assumptions and reporting revisit statistics.
In §2.4/Table 6, add an X-band link budget (EIRP, path loss, G/T, modulation/coding, margin) to verify the 50 Mbit/s downlink and 34 min usable contact.

In §2.2–2.4, add a risk/evidence note for the unflown Vega C baseline and rideshare dispersion without propulsion, and provide evidence or mitigation for assuming S/X-band at Mount Pleasant; also standardise bibliography entries.

criteria.C1: Your Introduction clearly states the GBR imaging mission, direct-detection rationale, single-spacecraft choice, AIMS operator and customers, with references. This is Accomplished. To secure the top of the band, tighten the link between customer needs and the 5 m visible requirement and ensure every rationale claim has a specific citation.
criteria.C2: Your §2.2–2.5 and Appendix A give strong evidence for launch, orbit, coverage, communications, manoeuvres and EOL. To strengthen within Accomplished, add an STK coverage/revisit analysis for Table 3, an X-band link budget for Table 6’s 50 Mbit/s and 34 min contact, and evidence/risk treatment for Vega C unflown status, rideshare dispersion without propulsion, and Mount Pleasant S/X-band capability.
criteria.C3: Your Conclusion is specific and evidence-based: it restates one 50 kg satellite meeting the need and candidly lists four limitations. This is Accomplished. To reach the top of the band, tie each limitation to a concrete risk or next design step and avoid introducing any new material not already supported in the main body.
criteria.C4: Your report has a clear engineering structure, concise Executive Summary, labelled figures/tables and matching citations. At 8/10 in Accomplished, the main gap is bibliography quality: several entries are incomplete or weakly formatted. To move toward the top of the band, standardise all references and check every in-text citation matches the list exactly.
